newsitem.title: USA: Body of Florida boy found in alligator's jaws.
newsitem.headline: Body of Florida boy found in alligator's jaws.

text.p: Trappers on Saturday recovered the body of a three-year-old boy from the jaws of an alligator that killed him while he was playing by a lake in central Florida.
'Gator trappers, who searched Lake Ashby all night looking for an alligator large enough to have taken a child, killed the 11-foot (3.3 metre) beast with three blasts from a shotgun.
The alligator, which was discovered one mile (1.6 km) from where Adam Binford disappeared on Friday, still had the boy's body in its jaws, authorities said.
"I never seen anything like it," trapper Roy Speck said.
"The boy was still in its jaws. He hadn't been eaten or anything. I just don't know what that 'gator was up to."

Adam was playing with his dog and picking petals off water lilies while his mother and older siblings ate at a picnic bench. His mother, Lorri Binford, heard a tremendous splash and turned to see the water churning, authorities said.
Alligator attacks on humans are rare and fatal attacks even more so.

Adam Binford was only the eighth person killed by an alligator since 1948, despite the fact that alligators can be found in nearly every body of water in Florida, said Lt. Joy Hill of the Florida Game and Freshwater Fish Commission.
Game officials believe the alligator may have been attracted by the boy's springer spaniel. The alligator's natural prey includes small mammals such as opossums and beavers.
